Repeatedly choosing among four variants and many checkpoints can overfit the same 800 validation users; checkpoint selection counts as model selection. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) show selection bias can rival differences between algorithms. Recommended plan: predeclare checkpoint frequency, stopping rules, comparison contrasts, and equal GPU-second budgets including tuning and failures; report performance against compute consumed. Equal epochs need not imply equal compute. Keep splits and seeds pinned, log every validation query, and reserve the host’s untouched held-out evaluation for confirmation. Fair comparisons must include tuning costs ([optimizer benchmarking study](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.11758)).

For uncertainty, apply a dataset-stratified paired user bootstrap: independently resample 200 users with replacement within each category, using identical sampled user indices across all variants; calculate each category’s mean hit indicator, then average the four means and record paired differences. Use approximately 10,000 replicates for 95% intervals; report category results and adjust confirmatory comparisons for multiplicity. This adapts standard [paired bootstrap guidance](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html). Intervals for selected checkpoints remain conditional on fitted models, fixed candidates, and observed datasets; they neither remove adaptive selection bias nor measure training-seed or negative-sampling uncertainty. Bootstrapping checkpoint selection can describe selection instability, but cannot create an independent confirmation set.

HR@10 against 99 negatives measures ranking within 100 candidates. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse model ordering relative to full-catalog metrics, even in expectation. Preserve the pinned evaluator; interpret gains narrowly. Inspect full-catalog unseen-item recommendations separately for the designated training users, without treating those qualitative diagnostics as held-out accuracy evidence.
